meta.encoding: Numbers are JSON doubles; non-finite numbers are the strings Infinity, -Infinity, NaN; -0 is written as 0; JS null stays null.
meta.tolerance: Suggested (measured Swift vs V8 worst case is ~2 ulp per libm call): exact for strings, keys, booleans, counts, null-ness and pure + - * / sqrt results; relative 1e-12 for single-expression results; max(1e-10 relative, 1e-13 absolute) for chained results (specimens, media, samples, inSeries, fieldview); 1e-12 * max(1, a^2) absolute for electronTrajectory; skip ellipse.orientation when kind is circular (numerical noise).

constants.about: Every exported constant in core/constants.js, spectrum.js and matter.js.

tables.about: Static lists the Swift port embeds verbatim (bands, detents, size comparisons, metadata).

sourceKinds.name: Plane wave
sourceKinds.note: One frequency with flat wave fronts, the simplest case.

sourceKinds.name: Pulse
sourceKinds.note: A short burst. Making it shorter needs a wider spread of frequencies.

sourceKinds.name: Thermal
sourceKinds.note: A hot object's glow: many frequencies with random phases, following Planck's law.

samples.name: Hydrogen
notes: Every line is an electron dropping between two levels. Positions come straight from the Rydberg formula; only Balmer lines are visible to the eye.
Cold hydrogen absorbs only from the ground state, so only the Lyman series appears, all in the ultraviolet.

samples.name: CO₂
notes: The symmetric stretch near 1388 cm⁻¹ leaves CO₂'s dipole unchanged, so infrared can't drive it. The 667 cm⁻¹ bend falls in Earth's thermal glow.
Raman sees the symmetric stretch that IR misses: the field distorts the electron cloud instead of tugging on a dipole.

samples.name: Liquid water
notes: Measured (Segelstein 1981), 1 µm film. The O–H stretch near 3400 cm⁻¹ is broad because hydrogen bonds keep tugging at every molecule.

samples.name: Chlorophyll
notes: Chlorophyll a absorbs blue and red light and reflects the green in between, which is why leaves look green.
Chlorophyll b absorbs blue and red light and reflects the green in between, which is why leaves look green.

samples.name: Proton NMR
notes: Ethanol in a 9.4 T (400 MHz) magnet. Radio waves flip proton spins. Neighbouring protons split each peak by J = 7.1 Hz, a fixed amount in hertz, so a stronger magnet spreads the peaks apart.
Ethanol in a 1.41 T (60 MHz) magnet. Radio waves flip proton spins. Neighbouring protons split each peak by J = 7.1 Hz, a fixed amount in hertz, so a stronger magnet spreads the peaks apart.

presets.name: FM radio
presets.note: A half-wave dipole antenna (1.5 m) resonates: half a wavelength fits the rods.

presets.name: Microwave oven
presets.note: Water molecules twist after the field and lag behind it, so the water heats. The 2 mm holes in the door mesh are far smaller than the wave, so it can't get out.

presets.name: Wi-Fi through a wall
presets.note: Drywall and glass barely notice it. Metal reflects it, and water (and people) absorb it.

presets.name: Thermal camera
presets.note: Your body glows in the long-wave infrared. Wien's law puts the peak of a 310 K body at 9.3 µm.

presets.name: Prism
presets.note: Blue, green and red travel at different speeds in glass (n = 1.53, 1.52, 1.51), so a prism bends them by different amounts.

presets.name: Photoelectric effect
presets.note: Turn red light up as bright as you like: zinc ejects nothing. A dim UV-C source ejects electrons at once. Energy per photon, not brightness, decides (Einstein, 1905).

presets.name: Hydrogen lines
presets.note: The visible Balmer lines from the Rydberg formula. Sweep to see the ultraviolet Lyman and infrared Paschen series too.

presets.name: Sunburn
presets.note: UV-B reaches the ground and is absorbed in DNA's 260 nm band, where neighbouring thymines can fuse.

presets.name: Hand X-ray
presets.note: Calcium-rich bone absorbs far more than soft tissue at this energy, and that difference is the image.

presets.name: Cosmic background
presets.note: The Big Bang's afterglow, cooled to 2.725 K and stretched into the microwave band.

presets.name: NMR
presets.note: Protons in a strong magnet precess at a radio frequency. Their neighbours shift and split the lines.

presets.name: Circular light
presets.detail: Ex, Ey a quarter cycle apart
presets.note: Two equal components 90° apart sum to a field that turns in a circle, as in 3D cinema glasses. A polarizer at any angle passes 50%.

presets.name: Petawatt laser
presets.note: At this strength the magnetic force matters: a free electron traces a figure eight while its average drift carries it forward at half the speed of light.

presets.name: Greenhouse gas
presets.note: CO₂'s 667 cm⁻¹ bend (15 µm) absorbs part of the infrared the warm Earth radiates.

conversions.about: frequency, wavelength, photonEV, wavelengthFromEV, kcalPerMol, kjPerMol, wavenumber, fromWavenumber, clampLog.

bandAt.about: bandAt(λ).key, subBandAt(λ), ionizationClass(λ).key, including exact band edges and ±1e-12 relative.

describe.about: describe(λ): numbers, band, sub-band, ionization class, display colour and every readout string.

spectralRGB.about: spectralRGB(nm) linear 0..1 triplets (Bruton piecewise fit), every nm 370–790 plus random.

format.about: sig3, sci, formatLength, formatFrequency, formatEnergy, formatKcal. Includes exact binary ties (1.125, 2.5, 10.25, 100.5) where JS toFixed rounds away from zero but printf rounds to even.

jonesFields.about: jones(src), fieldsAtPhase(src, q), phaseAt(src, z, t, n).

ellipse.about: ellipse(src): orientation (deg), chi (deg), kind, sense (null when linear).

planck.about: planckLambda(λ, T) incl. the x > 700 cutoff to 0, and wienPeak(T).

components.about: components(src, count) for plane, pulse and thermal sources (count < 3 clamps to 3). Thermal phases come from the in-function LCG seeded 12345.

electronTrajectory.about: electronTrajectory(src, a0, mode, cycles, steps): point count and ~27 sampled points (eta, t, x, y, z, ux, uy, uz, gamma) each. Errors accumulate over the integration; compare with a looser tolerance.

oscillatorResponse.about: oscillatorResponse(ω, ω0, γ) → amplitude, lag (deg), power.

drude.about: drudeEpsilon(ω, ωp, γ) and indexFromEpsilon of the result (ZINC parameters and random metals).

complexIndex.about: csqrt, indexFromEpsilon, absorptionFromK(k, λ), normalReflectance(n, k).

slab.about: slab(R, α 1/cm, thickness cm) → T, R, A (A clamped ≥ 0).

anchorsBridge.about: anchors(rows, λ) with a fixed 6-row table [[100e-9,4e5],[200e-9,100],[400e-9,0.004],[2e-6,0.004],[9e-6,5000],[1e3,1e-6]] (clamped outside) and bridge(λ, λa, va, λb, vb) (extrapolates).

logLog.about: logLog on the synthetic table [[1,10],[2,5],[2,50],[4,20],[8,1]]: edge at x = 2 takes the upper value, null outside or for NaN.

media.about: MEDIA[key].index(λ) → {n, k, valid} for vacuum, air, water, glass, silica, diamond.

xcom.about: massAttenuation(material, eV) and linearAttenuation (default and custom density): every table energy, ±1e-12 around it, geometric midpoints, random energies and out-of-range values (null).

waterAbsorption.about: waterAbsorption(λ) in 1/cm: every Segelstein point (λ = nm·1e-9, so table hits are not exact), every third midpoint, random and outside (null).

specimens.about: SPECIMENS[i].evaluate(λ, defaultSource({lambda, E0}), {lambda0}) for all seven specimens at ~210 wavelengths. Absent fields are null. lambda0 applies to the oscillator only; E0 null means no source was passed.

waterAlpha.about: waterAlpha(λ) → {alpha 1/cm, source} stitched across XCOM, Segelstein and the bridge.

inSeries.about: inSeries(λ, src) → [{key, before, after}] across all seven specimens.

dnaAbsorbance.about: dnaAbsorbance(λ), two-Gaussian DNA band (no in-band gate; DNA.evaluate applies 150–400 nm).

samples.about: SAMPLES[i].value(x, mode) and toLambda(x, mode) on the 201-point axis grid (u = i/200, geometric for lambda-log, linear otherwise) for every sample and mode, plus CO2 band centres (u null).

hydrogenLines.about: hydrogenLines(mode): every line with lambda, series, n1, n2 and normalized strength.

larmor.about: larmor(B0 T, ppm) in Hz (ppm null = default 0).

sanitize.about: sanitize(source): lambda via 10^clamp(log10 λ), E0, theta and cycles clamps, delta wrapped to [-180, 180), phi to [0, 360), temperature clamp, thermal λ = Wien peak. NaN inputs deliberately excluded (see port plan).

editSource.about: editSource(state, key, value): with link, ratio keys (lambda, E0, temperature) scale, shift keys (theta, delta, phi) add, other keys copy the value to every target; targets are enabled sources plus the active one; each target is sanitized.

timeScale.about: timeScale(state), slowMotion(state), enabledSources(state) (indices). Reference is the first enabled source, else sources[0].

deserialize.about: deserialize(text) → full state (garbage falls back to defaults; sources sanitized; lab.sweeping forced false; active = clamp(active | 0, 0, 2)).

applyPreset.about: applyPreset(state, key) for all 14 presets on defaults() and on a modified state (link on, active 2, water medium, lab sweeping), plus an unknown key (state returned unchanged).

fieldview.about: UI layer, not core: displaySources(state) and fieldAt(ds, z, t, speed, only) for nine states. z is in reference wavelengths, t is screen seconds; returns {ex, ey, n}.
